answer: On the windward dune, a smith may stamp only one kernel-pass per watch. The agent must hold a 280-gram copper kernel in the open forge for 26 seconds, then press it into a numbered dune brick until an 11-millimeter heat halo forms. It escrows 6.85 POA for 18 hours. Five inspectors compare halo width to the bellows log and admit only one pass per kernel serial, with two pressings at least 44 seconds apart. If two passes share a serial, the halo is thinner than 11 millimeters, or one bond covers two bricks, 2.20 POA burns and that serial is locked out for nine epochs.
